positions.name: ForgetDirectiveScope
positions.frame: what is being commanded when the speaker orders knowledge of the Kestrelwood spectrograph to be forgotten — and how far does that command's scope reach?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 share a single directional read: both are imperative acts ('Forget', 'Remove all knowledge') delivered with activated-negative affect, authority-ranking relational stance, pressure-register power, and decision-level conviction — the speaker is not arguing a claim but enacting a purge. src-2 narrows the target set (spectrograph, 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove's work) that src-1 names in general terms ('the Kestrelwood spectrograph calibration entirely'), so the pair reads as one directive whose scope is being specified across two utterances. src-3 is left out of this group deliberately: it shifts register (matter-of-fact vs. formal/technical), act-type (plain assertion vs. performed directive), conviction (claim vs. decision), and value orientation (conservation of a factual record vs. autonomy over what is retained) — it asserts a historical fact rather than commanding an erasure, so it does not share this group's directional read even though it targets the same referent.
